interactions.summary: The interviewer offers to connect Jiang's school with empathy-focused peers, lesson-plan support, and public panel discussions.

Jiang says his program is unusually empowering inside China, but parent pressure is intense, so the school needs a global network and direct student-to-student exchange to reinforce its values and widen horizons.
The interviewer agrees that the proposed discussions can be organized and recorded publicly.
The interviewer asks Jiang for his own metaphor of empathy rather than the usual 'standing in someone else's shoes' formula.
After briefly considering other images, Jiang settles on water as his metaphor because empathy pervades life, nourishes society, and functions as its basic sustaining medium.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang starts with an abandoned dolphin image before revising toward his final water metaphor, so the segment records live thinking rather than a single polished answer.

claims.claim: Jiang says his school's program is highly distinctive in China and that students feel more respected, empowered, and personally better inside it.

He argues that parent and social-circle pressure push Chinese families toward SAT study, memorization, and visible credential work, making empathy-centered practices like reading and African service learning harder to justify.

Jiang says his school needs connection with philosophically aligned schools abroad because a global network reinforces its values inside a difficult Chinese environment and broadens students' horizons toward empathy.
claims.temporal_scope: Current institutional strategy and request on 2012-03-16.

claims.claim: He says non-Western-educated students who have moved through both the mainstream Chinese system and his program are especially valuable witnesses to what empathy-centered reform changes.
claims.temporal_scope: Current evidentiary claim on 2012-03-16 about students in Jiang's program.

claims.claim: Jiang defines empathy metaphorically as water or air: a pervasive life-sustaining medium without which society cannot function.

signature_moments.moment: Chinese parental anxiety appears as a barrage of status questions: why America, why not SATs, why books, why Africa.
signature_moments.source_phrase: why is he not studying for the SAT right now ... why is he reading books and ... going to Africa
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It makes the social resistance to Jiang's program concrete and shows empathy work colliding with credential panic.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang treats a global school network not as branding but as moral reinforcement for a fragile experiment inside China.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we really want to be part of a global network
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The packet shifts empathy from an internal pedagogy to an international support structure.

signature_moments.moment: Empathy becomes water: society's equivalent of the substance that nourishes and composes life itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: if water is to the individual, then empathy is to society
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the interview's strongest reusable formulations and later anchors Jiang's claim that societies dehydrate without empathy.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's term for connecting his program with like-minded schools abroad so students and values are reinforced through live exchange rather than isolated theory.

chronology_notes.note: This packet moves from current parent pressure around Jiang's already-running program to his immediate 2012 effort to internationalize support and bring a current student into the conversation as evidence.
